questions.text:
Consider a Boolean function [latex]f(w,x,y,z) [/latex] such that

[latex]\begin{array}{lll} f(w,0,0,z) & = & 1 \\ f(1,x,1,z) & =& x+z \\ f(w,1,y,z) & = & wz +y \end{array}[/latex]

The number of literals in the minimal sum-of-products expression of [latex]f [/latex] is ________
questions.solution:
From the conditions:
- x = 0, y = 0 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] f = 1 (term [latex]\bar x\bar y[/latex])
- x = 1 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] f = wz + y
- x = 0, y = 1, w = 1 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] f = z

[latex]f=\bar x\bar y+xy+wz[/latex] satisfies all three (the case x = 0, y = 1, w = 0 is not fixed). It has 2 + 2 + 2 = 6 literals, and no shorter expression fits.

Answer: 6

questions.text: If the numerical value of a 2-byte unsigned integer on a little endian computer is 255 more than that on a big endian computer, which of the following choices represent(s) the unsigned integer on a little endian computer?
questions.solution:
Write the little-endian value as [latex]256h+l[/latex] (high byte h, low byte l). The same bytes read big-endian give [latex]256l+h[/latex].

Difference [latex]=255(h-l)=255\Rightarrow h=l+1[/latex].
- 0x6665: h = 0x66, l = 0x65 True
- 0x0100: h = 1, l = 0 True
- 0x0001 and 0x4243 have h = l [latex]-[/latex] 1 False

Answer: 0x6665 and 0x0100

questions.text: If [latex]x[/latex] and [latex]y[/latex] are two decimal digits and [latex](0.1101)_2 = (0.8xy5)_{10}[/latex], the decimal value of [latex]x+y[/latex] is ___________
questions.solution:
[latex](0.1101)_2=\frac12+\frac14+\frac1{16}=0.8125[/latex]

0.8xy5 = 0.8125 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] x = 1, y = 2 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] x + y = 3

Answer: 3

questions.text:
Which one of the following circuits implements the Boolean function given below?

[latex]f(x,y,z) = m_0+m_1+m_3+m_4+m_5+m_6[/latex]

where [latex]m_i[/latex] is the [latex]i^{th}[/latex] minterm.
questions.solution:
Select lines are y (s1) and z (s0), so input [latex]I_{2y+z}[/latex] must equal f with x free:
- yz = 00: m0 (x = 0), m4 (x = 1) both 1 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]I_0=1[/latex]
- yz = 01: m1, m5 both 1 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]I_1=1[/latex]
- yz = 10: m2 = 0, m6 = 1 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]I_2=x[/latex]
- yz = 11: m3 = 1, m7 = 0 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]I_3=\bar x[/latex]

Inputs (1, 1, x, x') = circuit A.

Answer: A

questions.text:
The format of the single-precision floating point representation of a real number as per the IEEE 754 standard is as follows:

[latex]\begin{array}{|c|c|c|} \hline \text{sign} & \text{exponent} & \text{mantissa} \\ \hline \end{array}[/latex]

Which one of the following choices is correct with respect to the smallest normalized positive number represented using the standard?
questions.solution:
Normalized numbers need exponent field from 1 to 254 (0 is for zero/denormals). The smallest normalized positive number has exponent 00000001 and mantissa all 0: [latex]1.0\times2^{1-127}=2^{-126}[/latex].

Answer: exponent = 00000001 and mantissa = 0[latex]\ldots[/latex]0
